action.description: Action object MUST contain a field `submission`, and MAY contain arbitrary additional information.

actTimeout.description: Maximum runtime (seconds) to obtain an action from an agent.

episodeSteps.description: Maximum number of steps in the episode.

includeLegalActions.description: If true, include legalActions and legalActionStrings in observations. Defaults to false since these can be derived from serializedGameAndState.

initialActions.description: Actions applied to initial state before play begins to set up starting position.

loadPresetHands.description: Repeated poker only. Load preset hand chance actions from preset_hands.jsonl.

openSpielGameName.description: The short_name of the OpenSpiel game to load.

openSpielGameParameters.description: Game parameters for Open Spiel game.

openSpielGameString.description: The full game string including parameters.

presetHands.description: Repeated poker only. List of per-hand chance action sequences to use instead of random chance.

runTimeout.description: Maximum runtime (seconds) of an episode (not necessarily DONE).

seed.description: Integer currently only used for selecting starting position.

useImage.description: If true, indicates the observation is intended to be rendered as an image. Note that currently the agent harness is responsible for the actual rendering; no image is passed in the observation.

useOpenings.description: Whether to start from a position in an opening book.

currentPlayer.description: ID of player whose turn it is.

legalActionStrings.description: List of OpenSpiel legal action strings. Only included if includeLegalActions is true.

legalActions.description: List of OpenSpiel legal action integers. Only included if includeLegalActions is true.

openSpielGameName.description: Short name of the OpenSpiel game.

playerId.description: ID of the agent receiving this observation.

serializedGameAndState.description: Enables reconstructing the Game and State objects.

remainingOverageTime.description: Total remaining banked time (seconds) that can be used in excess of per-step actTimeouts -- agent is disqualified with TIMEOUT status when this drops below 0.

Reasoning:
1. Only column 3 is partially filled: bottom (row 5) has our x, row 4 has o.
2. If we drop in column 3 now, the o at row 4 already blocks any vertical line for us, and we give up the chance to extend useful horizontal/diagonal threats elsewhere.
3. In solved Connect-4 theory, after the opening “center / center” trade, the winning continuation for the first player is to take one of the two columns adjacent to the centre (columns 2 or 4).  
   • This puts a second x on the bottom row, next to the existing centre x, creating immediate horizontal and diagonal potential.  
   • It keeps enough time to block any future vertical attempt by o in column 3 (we can still drop above o later if needed).  
4. Either column 2 or 4 is symmetric; picking column 2 is standard and equally strong.
5. All other columns are strictly inferior: they give up central control and offer o easier counter-play.

Therefore the optimal move is to drop our disk in column 2.

action.thoughts:
The current position is very early-game, with X holding an adjacent pair at the bottom of columns 2-3 and O holding a single disk at row 4 of column 3 (directly atop one X). No player has three-in-a-row yet, so no forced wins, blocks, or immediate threats exist. X will be able to extend their bottom-row pair into three consecutive disks on their next turn regardless of where O plays (the open ends at columns 1 and 4 cannot both be covered in one move), but three-in-a-row is not yet a win and can be answered by occupying one extension square on the subsequent turn.

In this regime, optimal play prioritizes central control and creation of one's own connected pairs for maximum future flexibility (horizontal, vertical, and both diagonal directions). Column 3 is the exact center of the 7-column board; dropping there immediately produces a vertical O-O pair at rows 3-4 of the central file while keeping all upper even-row cells open for later threats. This outweighs alternatives such as:
- Occupying column 2 at row 4 (creates a horizontal O-O but only at a lower level atop X's base, with less influence on the true center).
- Occupying column 4 or 1 at row 5 (merely interferes with one end of X's potential three but creates no new O-O pair of our own and leaves the center unclaimed).
- Any outer column (even lower influence, fewer diagonal prospects).

Center-first development preserves the highest branching factor for future winning lines while remaining fully defensible against X's inevitable bottom-row extension. Therefore the move is column 3.

Final Answer: 3
